intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that multiple epiphyseal dysplasia-2 (EDM2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding the alpha-2 chain of type IX collagen (COL9A2; 120260) on chromosome 1p33-p32.

checks.claim: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia-2 (EDM2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the COL9A2 gene, which encodes the alpha-2 chain of type IX collagen.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation screening of candidate regions revealed a novel point mutation at position -1 in the COL9A2 exon 3/intron 3 splicing region.
checks.explanation: The abstract links a COL9A2 mutation to EDM2 in this family and describes the protein as the alpha2-chain of type IX collagen. It does not explicitly say the mutation is heterozygous.

checks.claim: The COL9A2 gene is located on chromosome 1p33-p32.
checks.evidence_quote: COL9A2 was mapped to human chromosome 1p32.3-p33 using fluorescence in situ hybridization.
checks.explanation: The paper maps COL9A2 to 1p32.3-p33, which matches the draft's 1p33-p32 written at slightly lower resolution.

paragraphs.text: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) is an autosomal dominant osteochondrodysplasia. Its features are delayed and irregular ossification of the epiphyses, joint pain and stiffness starting in childhood, mild short stature or normal height, and early-onset osteoarthritis. In the COL9A2-related form (EDM2), the knees tend to be the most severely affected joints, while the hips are relatively spared.

checks.claim: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) is an autosomal dominant osteochondrodysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) is a dominantly inherited chondrodysplasia
checks.explanation: The abstract calls MED a dominantly inherited chondrodysplasia, which matches the claim.

checks.claim: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia is characterized by delayed and irregular ossification of the epiphyses.
checks.evidence_quote: It is suggested that this was caused by the fragmented and maldeveloped epiphyses characteristic of epiphyseal dysplasia.
checks.explanation: The abstract calls fragmented and maldeveloped epiphyses characteristic of the condition, which fits irregular epiphyses. It does not mention delayed ossification.

checks.claim: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia features joint pain and stiffness starting in childhood.
checks.evidence_quote: Beginning in childhood, the disease leads to pain and stiffness of knees, ankles, elbows and finger joints.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Individuals with multiple epiphyseal dysplasia have mild short stature or normal height.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by mild short stature and early-onset osteoarthrosis
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions mild short stature but says nothing about normal height.

checks.claim: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia features early-onset osteoarthritis.
checks.evidence_quote: Finally, affected individuals are prone to the development of early degenerative joint disease.
checks.explanation: Early degenerative joint disease is the same thing as early-onset osteoarthritis.

checks.claim: In COL9A2-related multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (EDM2), the knees tend to be the most severely affected joints.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. The knees are listed among the affected joints, but the abstract never says they are the most severely affected.

checks.claim: In COL9A2-related multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (EDM2), the hips are relatively spared.
checks.evidence_quote: a special subtype of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) in which the hips are not markedly affected at early age (EDM2)
checks.explanation: Hip sparing in EDM2 is stated.

paragraphs.text: EDM2 is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern, as shown by the multigenerational family used for the linkage study of Briggs et al. (1994).

checks.claim: EDM2 is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern, as shown by the multigenerational family used in the linkage study of Briggs et al. (1994).
checks.evidence_quote: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) is a dominantly inherited chondrodysplasia
checks.explanation: The abstract describes MED as dominant and the study family as large, but it never calls the family multigenerational or says the family itself shows the inheritance pattern.

paragraphs.text: Briggs et al. (1994) studied a large family with MED that did not show linkage to the chromosome 19 locus (EDM1). By linkage analysis, they mapped the disease locus to a region of chromosome 1p that contains COL9A2, the gene encoding the alpha-2 chain of type IX collagen.

checks.claim: Briggs et al. (1994) studied a large family with multiple epiphyseal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: Linkage studies with the chromosome 19 markers were carried out in a large family with MED
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the authors studied a large family with MED.

checks.claim: The large MED family studied by Briggs et al. (1994) did not show linkage to the chromosome 19 EDM1 locus.
checks.evidence_quote: Linkage studies with the chromosome 19 markers were carried out in a large family with MED and excluded the previously identified interval.
checks.explanation: The family excluded the chromosome 19 MED/PSACH interval. Calling that interval EDM1 is just standard naming.

checks.claim: By linkage analysis, Briggs et al. (1994) mapped the MED locus in their family to a region of chromosome 1p containing COL9A2, the gene encoding the alpha-2 chain of type IX collagen.
checks.evidence_quote: we have identified an MED locus on the short arm of chromosome 1, in a region containing the gene (COL9A2) that encodes the alpha 2 chain of type IX collagen
checks.explanation: The abstract maps the locus to 1p in a region containing COL9A2, as the claim says.

paragraphs.text: MED is genetically heterogeneous. Other autosomal dominant forms are caused by mutations in COMP (EDM1), COL9A3 (EDM3), MATN3 (EDM5), and COL9A1 (EDM6). An autosomal recessive form (EDM4) is caused by mutations in SLC26A2.

checks.claim: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: a form of MED have been linked to the same interval on chromosome 19 ... excluded the previously identified interval. Using this family, we have identified an MED locus on the short arm of chromosome 1
checks.explanation: Having separate MED loci on chromosome 19 and chromosome 1 directly shows genetic heterogeneity.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant multiple epiphyseal dysplasia EDM1 is caused by mutations in COMP.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. COMP and EDM1 are not mentioned.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant multiple epiphyseal dysplasia EDM3 is caused by mutations in COL9A3.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. COL9A3 and EDM3 are not mentioned.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant multiple epiphyseal dysplasia EDM5 is caused by mutations in MATN3.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. MATN3 and EDM5 are not mentioned.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant multiple epiphyseal dysplasia EDM6 is caused by mutations in COL9A1.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. COL9A1 and EDM6 are not mentioned.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive multiple epiphyseal dysplasia EDM4 is caused by mutations in SLC26A2.
checks.evidence_quote: Double-layered patella in multiple epiphyseal dysplasia is not exclusive to DTDST mutation.
checks.explanation: The title links DTDST (SLC26A2) mutation to MED. It does not mention recessive inheritance or the EDM4 designation.

paragraphs.text: Muragaki et al. (1996) studied the family originally reported by Briggs et al. (1994). They found that affected members were heterozygous for a splice site mutation in the COL9A2 gene. The mutation caused exon 3 to be skipped from the mRNA, which deletes 12 amino acids from the COL3 domain of the alpha-2(IX) chain while keeping the reading frame intact. This was the first report showing that a type IX collagen gene causes human disease.

checks.claim: Muragaki et al. (1996) studied the MED family originally reported by Briggs et al. (1994).
checks.explanation: The title does not mention the Briggs et al. (1994) family. Only the title was supplied.

checks.claim: Muragaki et al. (1996) found that affected members of the Briggs et al. (1994) MED family were heterozygous for a splice site mutation in the COL9A2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: A mutation in the gene encoding the alpha 2 chain of the fibril-associated collagen IX, COL9A2, causes multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (EDM2).
checks.explanation: The title reports a COL9A2 mutation but does not say it is a splice site mutation, that it is heterozygous, or which family was studied. Only the title was supplied.

checks.claim: The COL9A2 splice site mutation identified by Muragaki et al. (1996) caused skipping of exon 3 from the mRNA.
checks.explanation: The title does not mention exon 3 skipping. Only the title was supplied.

checks.claim: Skipping of COL9A2 exon 3 in the family studied by Muragaki et al. (1996) deletes 12 amino acids from the COL3 domain of the alpha-2(IX) chain.
checks.explanation: The title does not mention the 12-amino-acid deletion or the COL3 domain. Only the title was supplied.

checks.claim: Skipping of COL9A2 exon 3 in the family studied by Muragaki et al. (1996) keeps the reading frame intact.
checks.explanation: The title does not say whether the reading frame is preserved. Only the title was supplied.

checks.claim: The report by Muragaki et al. (1996) was the first to show that a type IX collagen gene causes human disease.
checks.explanation: The title does not say this was the first report of a type IX collagen gene causing human disease. Only the title was supplied.

paragraphs.text: Later studies of other families with MED also found heterozygous COL9A2 mutations that affect the exon 3 splice donor site and cause exon 3 to be skipped. This suggests that in-frame loss of exon 3 is a recurrent disease mechanism.

checks.claim: Later studies of other families with multiple epiphyseal dysplasia found heterozygous COL9A2 mutations affecting the exon 3 splice donor site.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation screening of candidate regions revealed a novel point mutation at position -1 in the COL9A2 exon 3/intron 3 splicing region.
checks.explanation: This paper reports a COL9A2 mutation at the exon 3 splice donor region in another MED family. The abstract does not explicitly say the mutation is heterozygous.

checks.claim: The COL9A2 exon 3 splice donor site mutations found in other MED families cause exon 3 skipping.
checks.evidence_quote: This G --> C substitution most probably induces an alteration of the splicing process.
checks.explanation: The abstract says the mutation only 'most probably' alters splicing and does not show that exon 3 is skipped in this family.

checks.claim: In-frame loss of COL9A2 exon 3 is suggested to be a recurrent disease mechanism in multiple epiphyseal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: Together with previous reports our results indicate that mutations leading to skipping of exon 3 within the COL3 domain of the alpha2-chain of collagen type IX may be relatively common in patients with a special subtype of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia
checks.explanation: The abstract supports exon 3 skipping as a recurrent mechanism. It does not say the exon loss is 'in-frame'.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Knee pain and stiffness, knees predominantly involved
